title: Quickfire Staging Playlab — Rehearsal Notes
content:
Purpose:
A short, transportable set of rehearsal cues and rapid roleplays for seller + SE practice. Goal is 10–15 minute lab sessions that improve: opening, one-minute value, 30s technical anchor, two top objections and a live fallback script. This doc is intentionally light — use it as the facilitator cue sheet.

Context / why this exists:
- We keep getting last-minute requests from enterprise prospects to show both economics and operational resilience.
- Sellers need a repeatable frame to run quick calls with SEs and Ops so they don’t over-index on features.
- This is a rehearsal-first complement to the heavier play decks (keeps momentum in field enablement).

Audience:
- Primary: Account Executive + Sales Engineer pairing (early pilot, mid-market, enterprise).
- Secondary: Pre-sales SDRs prepping demos, Solutions Engineers prepping for POC handoff.

Structure (10–15m session):
1) Warmup (2m): lightning context share — prospect industry, primary outcome, current host infra (SaaS / on-prem / VPC).
2) One-minute value (1m): seller practices 60s hook (see templates below).
3) Technical anchor (2m): SE gives a 30–45s latency/cost/reliability snapshot tailored to the buyer persona.
4) Objection block (6m): run 2 objections as roleplay (seller handles, SE or PM reads prospect persona).
5) Fallback & Close (2m): canned fallbacks + commit to next step.

One-minute value templates (pick one and customize):
- Outcome-first: "We help you ship consistent, predictable LLM features into product lines so your engineers stop firefighting inference cost and latency — typical wins are 40–60% token cost reduction on reranking-heavy flows and 2–3x improvement in 95th percentile latency."
- Risk-first: "We let you run models with single-pane ops and industry-grade fallbacks so your app stays online during model or region incidents — you get predictable fallback policies and a measurable cost/latency tradeoff."
- Platform-first (for platform teams): "Same API surface across hosted, reserved, and private installs — you can standardize on one runtime and migrate workloads without re-architecting."

30s technical anchor samples (SE scripts):
- Low-latency demo: "Typical CPU-bound chat setups on 16k context run at 200–350ms/token on our dedicated pools; with continuous KV caching and batching you'll see 30–50% fewer GPU tokens billed."
- Cost anchor for embeddings: "For embedding-heavy search, we recommend prefix caching + quantized models for cold-starts — we commonly move unit cost down by 2–3x with negligible impact on top-K quality."
- Private deploy note: "Private deployment uses a control plane in your VPC and optional HSM for keys; we give a connector for on-prem monitoring and a fallback route into hosted if you permit it."

Top 4 objections + short counters (practice scripts)
1) "We can host ourselves, why pay?"
  - Practice counter: "Totally valid. Most customers start doing that; the difference is ops delta: we reduce the cost/time you spend on optimizing kernels, autoscaling, KV cache tuning, and real outages. Think of us as the runtime + ops team you don't have to hire completely. If you want, we can run a lightweight 2-week cost baseline so you can compare apples-to-apples."
  - Example prompt to propose: "Run a 2-week baseline on your p99 emitter with our profiler (JIRA-SELL-1187) — we’ll show where batching and prefix cache reduce per-token spend."

2) "How do you handle model regressions / quality drift?"
  - Practice counter: "We tie evals to your prompt sets and alert on distribution drift; we also support blue/green rollouts and automatic fallback to proven model variants if quality dips during a rollout. We can share a sample quality-alert rule we use in pilots."

3) "We need full control on-prem for compliance."
  - Practice counter: "Understood. Our Private offering provides a customer-controlled control plane and optional air-gap deploys. We also sign SOC/ISO addenda and integrate with your KMS/HSM — we can map the checklist to your compliance hits in the first call."

4) "Latency spikes during peak times are unacceptable."
  - Practice counter: "We route by policy — latency-first lanes and cost-first lanes. For hard SLOs we recommend a dedicated pool with burst capacity; we also provide canary policies and circuit-breaker fallbacks to cheaper but compatible variants."

Rehearsal roleplay scripts (short):
- Scenario A: Fintech pilot, accuracy-sensitive reranker, 500ms p95 target
  - Seller opener (30s): quick problem, expected outcome, ask for permission to show tech anchor.
  - SE (30s): latency/cost anchor and fallback sketch.
  - Prospect (role): asks about compliance and what happens during model drift.
  - Seller/SE handle, agree next step: 2-week pilot scope + baseline.

- Scenario B: B2B search, embedding-heavy, cost-sensitive
  - Seller 60s value -> SE 30s technical -> Prospect: "What about cold-starts?" -> SE runs through prefix caching + warmup approach and pilot metrics to collect.

Facilitator cues (keep this sticky):
- Timebox strictly — call it out at start: "We'll do 12 minutes; we start with a 60s value and finish with a decision."
- Use the JIRA real-ticket as a followup (JIRA-SELL-1187).
- Emphasize measurable outcomes (cost %, latency ms, SLO wording).
- If argument drifts to roadmap, park it in a backlog note and redirect to pilot KPIs.

Short checklist for post-lab improvements:
- Capture two lines of feedback per roleplay (what landed, what flopped).
- Tag any tech gaps for eng with an owner (e.g., quantization FAQ, default batch size guidance).
- Update the quick scripts if sellers invent new phrasing that works.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add a 2-slide mini-deck for the "One-minute value" that sellers can paste into email? (TODO: Rosa to draft by 2025-02-02)
- Should we record 3 exemplar roleplays and add to the SE enablement repo? (Devon to scope)
- Get legal to confirm a short private-deploy checklist we can share (Nora looped).

Notes to self:
- Keep language outcome-first and avoid product laundry lists during the 60s value.
- Practice language around fallback economics — sellers confuse "fallback" with "downgrade"; emphasize graceful degradation and transparency on unit costs.

Session logistics (ops):
- Recommended cadence: weekly 30m lab with two 12m runs + 6m debrief for early hires.
- Template invite: brief context + persona + one prioritized objection.
- Recording: optional, add to github.com/redwood-inference/demo-scripts/quickfire (linked above).

Appendix: quick cheat lines (one-liners to memorize)
- "We reduce per-token spend through smart caching and batching while keeping your worst-case latency bounded."
- "We give the same API, whether you run in our cloud, your VPC, or on-prem."
- "Our rollouts are canary-first and fallback-aware — you won’t wake up to a major quality regression without an automatic safety net."

End.
